Claim: LightGBM model outperforms Naive persistence on majority of individual commodities
Evidence: LightGBM P50 achieves lower MAE than persistence in 7 of 10 commodity markets; the observed MAE improvement ranges from 5.87% to 22.36% among those seven markets.
Result: 7 of 10 commodities improve; aggregate MAE is higher because Chilli Red, Mustard, and Gram(Chana) are difficult cases.

Claim: Ridge Linear Regression achieves lowest aggregate point forecast error
Evidence: Ridge achieves MAE of Rs 56.58/qtl and RMSE of Rs 113.60/qtl on the 2025 test set, with statistically significant differences versus LightGBM under the documented DM tests.
Result: Ridge MAE = Rs 56.58/qtl versus LightGBM P50 Rs 82.00/qtl; LightGBM versus Ridge MAE DM statistic = -8.0941, p < 0.001.
Allowed in Paper?: Yes (Reported honestly as linear point-forecast baseline)

Claim: Multi-source features provide incremental predictive power
Evidence: Feature ablation reports MAE of 116.76 without price lags, 83.36 without arrivals, 81.96 without festivals, and 82.00 for the full LightGBM P50 reference.
Result: Price history is the strongest signal; arrivals and festivals provide smaller complementary effects in this ablation.

Claim: Prediction intervals achieve nominal 80% coverage via Conformal Quantile Regression
Evidence: Mondrian CQR achieves 79.49% empirical coverage on the untouched 2025 test set against an 80.0% nominal target, with MPIW of Rs 228.78/qtl.
Result: 79.49% empirical coverage and zero post-rearrangement quantile crossings on the 2025 test set.

Claim: Model demonstrates spatial generalization across Indian agricultural markets
Evidence: Leave-One-Mandi-Out results cover all 10 holdout mandis; MAE ranges from Rs 15.14/qtl at Khanna to Rs 276.53/qtl at Azadpur.
Result: Spatial transfer is nonuniform: strongest at Khanna and Karnal, with materially larger degradation at Azadpur, Guntur, Indore, and Kolkata.

Claim: Price series non-stationarity is verified and addressed via lag differences/EMAs
Evidence: ADF and KPSS diagnostics are reported per commodity; the direct price-level Ridge benchmark has MAE Rs 56.58/qtl, while the delta formulation has MAE Rs 56.00/qtl.
Result: The delta formulation is close to the raw-price formulation; the study retains the canonical raw-price contract for the primary benchmark.

Claim: Exogenous agricultural drivers share Granger-predictive association with modal prices
Evidence: Grouped Granger testing with BH-FDR correction finds arrivals significant in 100.00% of series groups, maximum temperature in 92.45%, and rainfall in 60.38%.
Metric/Experiment: Grouped Granger Causality with BH-FDR Correction
Result: These are statistical predictive associations, not evidence of physical causation.

Claim: Deep learning models conclusively underperform GBDT across all conditions
Evidence: Deep-learning benchmark metrics and training configurations are sourced from the current benchmark artifacts; results are interpreted according to the documented tuning scope.
Result: Sequence models show higher error under default parameters; DL is classified as proof-of-concept baseline.
Allowed in Paper?: No (Must be qualified as proof-of-concept comparison)

Claim: Isolation Forest is a validated 95%+ accurate supervised anomaly detector
Evidence: Evaluated against operational heuristic proxy rules, not verified historical ground-truth events.
Result: Unsupervised operational triage indicator; qualitative historical case studies provided.
Allowed in Paper?: No (Must be framed as unsupervised operational triage tool)

Claim: Model is proven robust to unseen global pandemics (COVID stress test)
Evidence: COVID-era data (2020-2021) was included in the training pool.
Result: In-sample retrospective consistency check (MAE Rs 29.42 in 2020-2021 vs Rs 33.67 in 2022-2024).
Confidence: High (As in-sample consistency) / False (As unseen test)
Allowed in Paper?: No (Must be framed as in-sample regime consistency)
